newsitem.title: UK: Major may face political trouble over airport tax.
newsitem.headline: Major may face political trouble over airport tax.

text.p: A potential new threat to Prime Minister John Major loomed on Wednesday as the Ulster Unionist Party and the Scottish Nationalist Party joined forces to try to defeat government plans to double Britain's airport departure tax.
UUP leader David Trimble and SNP leader Alex Salmond said they would launch a campaign on Thursday to build a cross-party coalition in an attempt to defeat the proposal.
The nine UUP MPs -- from Northern Ireland -- hold the balance of power in the lower House of Commons, where Major's 322 Conservatives are exactly matched by 322 opposition members.
Salmond said it was impossible to say exactly when MPs would get a chance to vote on the airport tax, which is part of the finance bill to implement the 1997/98 budget.
The bill is presently in its committee stage in the House of Commons.

Salmond said he hoped the main opposition Labour Party would oppose the tax increase, rather than abstain, once it realised the issue presented a good opportunity to inflict an embarrassing defeat on the government so close to a general election. An election has to be held by May 22.
The UUP and SNP say the proposed tax rise would be especially hard on those people from Northern Ireland and Scotland who have little alternative but to take planes.
